back: Guide the team with integrity, make responsible decisions, and take ownership of the project's objectives, actions and decisions.
Authority: a position of control granted by the organization. Leadership: inspiring and motivating others by example. Anyone can lead.

front: Five characteristics of an accountable leader
back: Integrity, honesty and fairness; self-awareness; respectfulness, humility and availability; flexibility and adaptability; shared leadership.
Leadership is not exclusive to one role. A team member or stakeholder may lead at different moments. Common on high-performing projects.
Leading by working for the team: being open to feedback, supporting their needs and removing barriers.
Understanding your own motives, values, feelings and strengths, and how they connect to your actions.
An environment where people can speak up, ask questions and admit mistakes without fear. Leaders are expected to foster it.

front: Why do projects need more leadership than operations?
back: They join groups that do not normally work together, carry higher stakes, and attract many influencers, which creates confusion and conflict.
Meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

front: Sustainability pyramid, most to least desirable
back: Avoid, minimize, restore, compensate/offset.
Social equity, environmental stewardship, economic prosperity: people, planet, profit.

front: Who is accountable for sustainability in a project?
back: Project managers, teams and sponsors, jointly.
A side effect the project creates for others, such as pollution or disruption. The sustainability principle asks for a strategy to address it.

front: Where can sustainability goals be formally recorded?
back: As KPIs in the project charter, business case, scope statement or contracts, confirmed by the sponsor.

front: Three challenges of sustainability in projects
back: Broader time horizon and more stakeholders (cost, complexity); sustainability risks when factors are unbalanced; no universal success criteria.
Foster proactive collaboration and unity around shared objectives among stakeholders and teams with diverse skills, knowledge and experience.

front: What does an empowered culture require?
back: Mutual trust, and full clarity on roles, responsibilities, team agreements and guiding processes.
Behavioral parameters and working norms set by the team itself at the beginning of the project, upheld by individual and team commitment.

front: Five areas of an empowered culture
back: Diversity, process definition, interpersonal skills, knowledge of organizational structures, team agreements.

front: Why is an empowered culture harder for virtual teams?
back: Different work styles and time zones, and no in-person interaction, make collaboration and relationship building harder.

front: PMI's preferred first response to conflict
back: Collaborate to find the root cause and a workable solution, before enforcing contracts or escalating.
